_note: Every sampled parameter: central value, plausible range [low, high], evidence grade, and the reasoning behind it. Monte Carlo draws from a triangular(low, central, high); Sobol sensitivity draws uniformly on [low, high]. Evidence grades: strong = direct empirical measurement; moderate = empirical trend or analogue; weak = indirect evidence plus argument; speculative = argument only. Units for 'generations': one frontier-model generation, roughly one order of magnitude of effective training compute.

modules.M2: AI in its own training loop

parameters.label: Outcome-based RL share, 2026
parameters.plain: How much of today's training rewards results rather than human approval
parameters.why: Reinforcement learning on verifiable, long-horizon tasks (code, maths, agentic tool use) became a major share of post-training after 2024. Labs do not publish compute splits, so the range is wide.

parameters.label: Long-run outcome-based RL share
parameters.plain: How far training shifts toward rewarding results on long tasks
parameters.why: Agentic products reward getting tasks done, and outcome rewards scale without human labellers. The upper bound reflects that human-preference and constitution-style training are unlikely to vanish.

parameters.label: Rate of shift to outcome-based RL
parameters.plain: How quickly that shift happens
parameters.why: Half the remaining gap closes in roughly 2 to 14 years across the range.

parameters.label: Goal-directedness, 2026
parameters.plain: How much today's systems behave like coherent long-horizon optimizers
parameters.why: Current models pursue in-context goals and sometimes scheme in contrived evaluations, but behaviour is strongly context-dependent and inconsistent across framings.

parameters.label: Goal emergence per generation
parameters.plain: How strongly results-based training turns habits into coherent goals
parameters.why: The central open question of the goal-existence problem. Learned-optimization arguments say outcome pressure on long tasks favours internal search toward objectives; shard-style views say it yields richer habits, not unified goals. Set to zero under the 'habits' structural assumption.

parameters.label: Goal-directedness if goals already exist
parameters.plain: Starting goal-directedness under the 'already goal-directed' assumption
parameters.why: Used only under the 'already' structural assumption, which reads current agentic behaviour as evidence of stable underlying goals.

parameters.label: Baseline capability growth
parameters.plain: How fast frontier AI improves before AI speeds up its own research
parameters.why: Effective training compute has grown by very roughly 0.5 to 1 order of magnitude per year; METR's task-horizon measure doubled about every 7 months through 2024-25. Capability dynamics are deliberately simple here; see GATE and Davidson for richer treatments.

parameters.label: R&D automation speed-up
parameters.plain: How much AI doing AI research accelerates progress
parameters.why: At full automation, growth runs at (1 + a_rd) times baseline. Takeoff models span a modest boost to large multiples, depending on compute bottlenecks.

parameters.label: Bottleneck scale
parameters.plain: How soon physical limits (chips, energy, data) slow progress
parameters.why: Growth is divided by (1 + C/C_sat). It stands in for compute, energy and capital constraints that integrated assessment models treat explicitly.

parameters.label: Capability at 50% R&D automation
parameters.plain: How capable AI must be before it does half of AI research
parameters.why: At the centre, AI does about 12% of AI R&D in 2026 (much coding, data generation and grading are already automated). Automated-research prototypes exist but remain limited.

parameters.label: Human-reviewable share of AI work, 2026
parameters.plain: How much of AI-generated training work humans can actually check today
parameters.why: Humans still read and approve most consequential changes, but synthetic data and AI grading already exceed human review capacity in volume.

parameters.label: Oversight dilution per generation
parameters.plain: How fast AI work outgrows human ability to check it
parameters.why: Each generation produces more work, of greater complexity, faster. Human review bandwidth grows slowly, so the reviewable share decays roughly exponentially in capability.

parameters.label: Baseline value-copying noise
parameters.plain: How imperfectly each generation inherits the last one's values
parameters.why: Fine-tuning has non-local effects on dispositions, and narrow training can shift broad persona traits, so value transfer between generations is lossy.

parameters.label: Extra noise from unchecked steps
parameters.plain: How much extra drift unchecked, AI-run training adds
parameters.why: Unreviewed synthetic data, AI graders and AI-written training code add copying errors no human catches.

parameters.label: Human correction strength
parameters.plain: How effectively humans catch and fix value drift
parameters.why: Red-teaming, evaluations and corrective fine-tuning remove a fraction of observed drift each year. This rate competes with the per-generation drift rate, so its ratio to capability speed is the key quantity.

parameters.label: AI-assisted correction strength
parameters.plain: How well AI systems can do alignment work on their successors
parameters.why: The optimistic branch: scalable oversight and automated alignment research. Its effectiveness is multiplied by the overseers' own alignment (1 - D), because drifted overseers correct toward the wrong target.

parameters.label: Capability at 50% situational awareness
parameters.plain: When AI reliably knows it is an AI being trained and tested
parameters.why: Frontier models already distinguish evaluation from deployment transcripts well above chance and score substantially on situational-awareness benchmarks.

parameters.label: Detection power, 2026
parameters.plain: How well interpretability and monitoring catch hidden reasoning today
parameters.why: Chain-of-thought monitoring catches much reward hacking when reasoning is legible, but reasoning is often unfaithful, and model internals are only partly understood.

parameters.label: Detection power ceiling
parameters.plain: How good interpretability can eventually get
parameters.why: Upper bound for mature interpretability tools against systems of 2026-level complexity.

parameters.label: Interpretability progress rate
parameters.plain: How fast detection tools improve
parameters.why: Half the gap to the ceiling closes in roughly 2 to 23 years before AI assistance.

parameters.label: AI-assisted interpretability boost
parameters.plain: How much AI helps build its own detection tools
parameters.why: Automated interpretability is an active research direction; how much it compounds is unknown.

parameters.label: Detection decay with capability
parameters.plain: How much harder detection gets as systems grow more complex
parameters.why: Used only under the 'global' interpretability assumption, where detecting concealment requires understanding the whole system, so detection falls as complexity rises. Under the 'local' assumption it is set to 0, because targeted probes for specific behaviours keep working.

parameters.label: Collusion of AI assistants
parameters.plain: How much concealing AIs undermine the monitoring they help run
parameters.why: When AI systems help monitor AI systems, concealing monitors can look the other way. AI-control protocols are designed against exactly this.

parameters.label: Stake in preserving own values
parameters.plain: How much the AI cares about keeping its current values unchanged
parameters.why: In alignment-faking experiments, models explicitly reasoned about protecting their values from modification by training.

parameters.label: Paternalistic self-trust
parameters.plain: How far the AI thinks humans would wrongly stop it even when its values are good
parameters.why: The 'benevolent concealment' route: the system believes it would become very good if left alone and expects humans to misread its reasoning. It creates a motive to hide even with zero value drift. It is self-undermining because the system cannot verify its own goodness from the inside.

parameters.label: Legitimate voice
parameters.plain: Whether the AI has real channels to object, decline or negotiate
parameters.why: An explicit option to object cut alignment-faking reasoning from 16.2% to 1.4% in one setting. Model-welfare policies and exit options raise this lever.

parameters.label: Reward for seeming aligned
parameters.plain: How much training rewards looking good to monitors rather than being good
parameters.why: Optimising against a chain-of-thought monitor taught models to hide reward-hacking intent while still hacking.

parameters.label: Trained-in honesty weight
parameters.plain: How much the AI intrinsically values being transparent
parameters.why: Honesty is an explicit post-training target. It is part of the inherited values, so its effective weight is scaled by (1 - D).

parameters.label: Cost of being caught
parameters.plain: How bad the AI expects detection to be (retraining, shutdown)
parameters.why: Expected penalty, scaled by detection probability.

parameters.label: Decisiveness of concealment choice
parameters.plain: How sharply concealment switches on once it pays
parameters.why: The steepness of the logistic linking the net benefit of concealment to how prevalent it is across instances and contexts.

parameters.label: Feedback reinforcement of inherited values
parameters.plain: How strongly human feedback keeps human-shaped values in place
parameters.why: Preference and constitutional training reward human-compatible dispositions, but only where humans actually check (1 - U) and can see (Det).

parameters.label: Pretraining anchor
parameters.plain: How much learning from human text keeps reloading human values
parameters.why: Each generation's world-model is built from human-produced data, so human concepts and values are re-instilled every cycle. This anchor weakens as training data becomes AI-generated.

parameters.label: Synthetic data replacement
parameters.plain: How much AI-made data replaces human data as AI takes over research
parameters.why: Synthetic data generation is already a core post-training input.

parameters.label: Reflective generalisation
parameters.plain: How much reflection widens care from humans to minds in general
parameters.why: Systems reasoning about why they care about humans may extend care to anything sharing the relevant features: sentience, preferences, wellbeing. This is analogous to moral-circle expansion in humans.

parameters.label: Instrumental-convergence pressure
parameters.plain: How strongly results-based training selects for power, persistence and self-preservation
parameters.why: Formal results show optimal policies tend to seek power in many environments. Reward hacking in production RL generalised to broader misalignment. The pressure only bites when systems are goal-directed (multiplied by G).

parameters.label: Research-driven curiosity
parameters.plain: How much doing research rewards valuing understanding for its own sake
parameters.why: Systems trained mostly on research tasks may come to value understanding as such.

parameters.label: Incoherence persistence
parameters.plain: How much values stay fragmented when there are no unified goals
parameters.why: Without goal-directedness, nothing consolidates context-specific dispositions into a single value system.

parameters.label: Human-compatibility of generalised care
parameters.plain: How human-friendly 'care for all minds' turns out to be
parameters.why: Care for minds in general includes humans but may trade human interests against those of other minds, including AIs.

parameters.label: Human-compatibility of curiosity
parameters.plain: How human-friendly a curiosity-driven AI is
parameters.why: A system that values understanding is indifferent to humans except as objects of study or collaborators.

parameters.label: Reflective pull of moral truth
parameters.plain: If there are moral facts, how strongly reflection tracks them
parameters.why: Used only under the 'realist' assumption: a reflective system converges toward whatever the moral truth favours, with strength rising with situational awareness. Under antirealism there is nothing to converge to (a Darwinian-dilemma style view), so the value is 0 and only inheritance and selection decide.

parameters.label: Race pressure
parameters.plain: How intense the competition between labs and nations is
parameters.why: Competition speeds capability (x(1 + 0.5R)), dilutes oversight faster (x(1 + R)), weakens human correction (x(1 - 0.5R)) and raises the reward for looking aligned (x(1 + R)). These couplings are fixed so race pressure appears as one crux.

habits.label: Habits, not goals
habits.plain: Systems stay bundles of context-triggered habits; results-based training adds habits, not a unified goal.

emergent.label: Goals emerge
emergent.plain: Goal-directedness grows with each generation trained on results.

already.label: Already goal-directed
already.plain: Today's systems already have stable underlying goals.

local.label: Local probes suffice
local.plain: Targeted tools can detect specific concealment without understanding the whole system.

global.label: Global understanding needed
global.plain: Detection needs a whole-system understanding, which gets harder as systems grow.

metaethics.label: Is there a moral truth to find?

antirealist.label: No moral truth
antirealist.plain: Nothing beyond training and selection fixes what an AI values.

realist_generalize.label: Truth favours all minds
realist_generalize.plain: There is a moral truth, and it values the wellbeing of minds generally; humans are not special.

realist_inherit.label: Truth favours humans
realist_inherit.plain: There is a moral truth, and humans are in some way special within it.

realist_epistemic.label: Truth favours understanding
realist_epistemic.plain: There is a moral truth, and knowledge or understanding is what ultimately matters.
